title: Risk capital is rentable between Prime Agents, so a Prime's capacity is not bounded by its own balance sheet
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.2.1.3.2 requires a Prime Agent to show how its Total Risk Capital covers a new Instance's Required Risk Capital, and enumerates the ways it may close a shortfall: renting Prime-External Junior Risk Capital from other Primes through Ecosystem Accords; sourcing Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital from external providers; originating Senior Risk Capital through the Sky monthly auction or renting OSRC from other Primes; bolstering Internal Junior Risk Capital through retained earnings; or "decreasing exposure in an existing Instance(s) to lower Aggregate RRC."

The structural claim is that risk-bearing capacity is a **tradeable input** rather than a property of a Prime. A Prime with an opportunity but no capital can rent capacity from a Prime with capital but no opportunity, which decouples who finds yield from who underwrites it and lets the ecosystem's total capital chase the best available use.

A.2.2.10.1.1.2.1.2 shows this reaching back into the earliest planning stage: before any proposal exists, the Prime "reaches out to other Prime Agents that could provide Junior Risk Capital (JRC) / Senior Risk Capital (SRC) or assume Asset Liability Management obligations." Deal-making with peers is part of feasibility, not an afterthought.

The containment is the sourcing ratios: the strategy must show compliance with rules "that constrain how much Senior Risk Capital can be 'enabled' or counted toward a Prime's Aggregate RRC." Without that cap, a Prime could fund unlimited exposure with the cheapest and least loss-absorbing tranche — the ratios are what keep rentable capital from becoming leverage.
description: A TRC coverage strategy may source Junior Risk Capital from other Primes or external providers via Ecosystem Accords, buy Senior Risk Capital at Sky's monthly auction, or shrink another Instance
